articles.title: Planning a multi-seller LoloBuy order around warehouse dates and open returns
articles.description: Decide which stored goods can wait for consolidation and which need a seller decision before the next parcel.

sections.heading: Start with the oldest received item
paragraphs: LoloBuy advertises 180 days of free storage and lets users combine selected stored goods from different sellers. That is useful when orders arrive at different times. It does not answer how long a seller will accept a return or how quickly a later seller will dispatch. Keep the warehouse dates and any applicable return dates in separate fields.

Suppose a coat arrives first, a scarf arrives a week later, and a small bag remains with its seller. The coat’s warehouse photos show a different lining from the one described. Before deciding whether to wait for the bag, resolve the lining question. Keeping a coat for months at no storage charge is poor value if the relevant seller action can expire much earlier.

sections.heading: Give each item a decision date
paragraphs: For the coat, record the discrepancy, the date of warehouse intake, the seller’s current terms and the action available in the order. For the scarf, note that it is ready and whether you have any delivery deadline. For the unshipped bag, record the seller’s latest confirmed event rather than entering a guessed arrival date. This makes the uncertainty visible.

Check the storage clock in your account, especially for goods processed on different dates. If an expiry date is unclear, ask about the specific item reference. Do not infer that placing a new order resets an earlier item’s clock or that the advertised free period gives permission to leave an item unreviewed indefinitely.

sections.heading: Price the choice to wait
paragraphs: Compare the parcel you can send today with the combination you might send after the bag arrives. Include a second shipment if the bag will travel separately; leave it out only if your actual alternative is to cancel or forgo the bag where that is possible. If you have only provisional dimensions, label the combined price as provisional.

Revisit the decision when an event changes: the seller dispatches, a product is found defective, a route closes, or the oldest item approaches its deadline. A useful plan does not require knowing the missing seller’s arrival date. It requires knowing what you will send if the bag still has not arrived when waiting no longer suits your priorities.

sections.heading: Build a timeline around decisions you can still change
paragraphs: Start with a small calendar for the coat, scarf and bag. Add the order date, shown warehouse receipt date, any seller action deadline and your own latest acceptable shipment date. Leave a blank when you have no verified date. A blank makes the uncertainty easy to spot. Filling it with an optimistic guess creates a false sense that the order is under control, particularly if you later copy the calendar into a parcel plan.

Sort the received items by the earliest date that requires an action, rather than by the date you purchased them. A newly received coat with a visible mismatch can require attention sooner than an older scarf whose inspection is complete. If the seller allows a specific response window, note where that information came from and whether the current order gives a deadline or only general wording. When in doubt, ask promptly and record the reply.

For the unreceived bag, keep the seller’s dispatch status separate from any courier estimate. A new tracking label is progress, but a physical acceptance scan gives stronger evidence that the seller has handed something over. A delivery scan at the destination warehouse is another step, while a matching stored item and reviewed photos are what let you decide whether it is suitable for international shipment. Avoid setting a firm plan that assumes all those steps happen simultaneously.

sections.heading: Make a fair cost comparison when one item is unresolved
paragraphs: A common mistake is to price the two ready items today and compare their quote with a future combined price that omits the unresolved item’s packaging. If the bag is structured, a rigid retail box could determine the combined parcel dimensions. If it is soft and can be folded without damage, the effect might be smaller. Ask what packaging could be acceptable and calculate a low and high scenario. Be explicit that you do not yet know which one applies.

Suppose the scarf alone could fit in a small envelope-style pack, the coat already needs a box, and the bag may push the box into another route or size band. The incremental effect of adding the scarf to the coat is different from the incremental effect of adding the bag. Price the combinations that match your real choices. Sending all three, sending coat and scarf now plus bag later, and waiting only for a seller answer about the coat are distinct plans.

If the coat is returned and you choose a replacement, include the timing and route uncertainty of the replacement in a new comparison. Do not continue using the old three-item quote after the contents change. If you give up the purchase entirely, keep the seller refund and the shipping plan in separate records. A reduction in the amount spent on goods is not a saving produced by warehouse consolidation.

sections.heading: Use the storage period well without postponing every decision
paragraphs: Long advertised free storage can be genuinely useful. A buyer might need time for independent orders to arrive, to compare two options from different sellers, or to confirm the destination address after a move. Use the period to collect the information that will improve the shipment. If every item is accepted and the final route is already affordable, waiting for an undefined future bargain may add little value.

Where a delivery date matters, work backward from the latest date you can accept the goods, leaving room for the uncertainty stated in the route estimate. A warehouse deadline several months away is irrelevant if you will move abroad next week and cannot receive the parcel at the old address. Check recipient details again at submission. The right shipping time is determined by the combination of warehouse conditions and your actual ability to receive the goods.

If an old item approaches its displayed deadline, ask the platform what options and costs apply before that deadline. Do not extrapolate from another buyer’s extension or assume a later account top-up resets the timer. Provide the specific warehouse item, its shown date and the action you are considering. If an extension is offered, save the new date and any fee and use them in your comparison.

sections.heading: Close each record once the item moves on
paragraphs: When the scarf joins an international parcel, attach the new parcel reference to its row and mark the warehouse decision complete. When the coat goes back to the seller, replace “stored” with the confirmed return status and keep tracking any outstanding refund. Leave the bag pending until it reaches a stage you can actually verify. These small changes prevent a returned item from accidentally appearing in a future packing plan.

A month later, the records should answer three simple questions: which items are still in storage, which unresolved deadlines remain, and which money or delivery events are still pending. If those answers are obvious, the advertised free period has served its purpose. You have gained flexibility without confusing separate sellers, parcel costs or return decisions.

If your plan is shared with a friend, send them the item-specific status rather than an account screenshot containing unrelated personal details. Explain which purchase is ready, which is awaiting a seller response, and which date will trigger a shipping decision. This lets them approve a split or a delay without mistakenly believing all three goods are already stored.

articles.title: How to measure an awkward LoloBuy parcel for the shipping calculator
articles.description: Use the packed outside dimensions and gross weight to compare shipping scenarios for a light product with an awkward shape.

sections.heading: Measure the smallest box you can actually use
paragraphs: A rolled poster and a small art book illustrate the problem. The poster is light but sets a minimum parcel length. The book may need a corner protector that increases width. Adding the product dimensions together in three directions creates a fictional carton. Instead, sketch how the objects can be packed with adequate protection and measure the outside dimensions of that arrangement.

LoloBuy’s estimator asks for grams and centimetres, the destination and the goods category. A measuring tape wrapped around a tube gives its circumference, not the width of the outer carton. If the final package is cylindrical or has an irregular shape, ask how the available carrier wants it measured. Do not assume every route will accept the shape at all.

sections.heading: Compare physically possible arrangements
paragraphs: For illustration, a 65 by 12 by 12 cm carton takes up 9,360 cubic centimetres. A rectangular carton measuring 65 by 25 by 12 cm takes up 19,500 cubic centimetres. Adding a narrow book might double the outer volume even if the total weight barely changes. This is geometry, not a LoloBuy billing formula. Enter the appropriate dimensions into the official estimate to see the route-specific result.

Now price two parcels if shipping separately is genuinely an option. Use a protected package size and gross weight for each, and sum both estimates. A lightweight tube might have few eligible routes. A heavier book might be compact enough to travel on a different route. The better choice depends on these actual results and the protection you need.

sections.heading: Revisit the estimate when packing changes
paragraphs: If a poster cannot be folded, include “keep rolled” in any request about compact packing. If the book is a gift, specify whether its original sleeve and corners must remain intact. Ask what outside size the warehouse expects under those instructions, then replace provisional measurements with actuals when available.

Compare the final result with the version of the quote that used the same contents and packaging. If the price rose, check whether the cause was the outside size, total weight, change in route or a separate service. The difference may have more than one cause. Keep the dated values so a support question can identify exactly which comparison needs explaining.

sections.heading: Check whether the product length determines the carton length
paragraphs: A poster advertised as 60 cm wide may fit a tube longer than 60 cm once the roll, protective wrapping and end caps are included. A 60 cm item measurement cannot automatically be entered as the packed length. Ask whether the seller’s figure describes the printed area, the sheet itself, the retail tube or the final shipping package. Even a trustworthy figure can be the wrong input if it describes a different object.

For a rolled product, establish which dimension actually runs along the tube. A seller may describe a poster as 60 by 90 cm but roll it so that the tube length follows the shorter edge, or supply it in a fixed retail tube that determines the length regardless of your preferred arrangement. If the artwork must remain in its original packaging, tell the warehouse. Changing the roll direction may alter the risk of creasing or simply be unavailable.

Two packages with equal volume can also have different maximum sides. A carton 80 by 10 by 10 cm occupies 8,000 cubic centimetres, as does one measuring 40 by 20 by 10 cm. A long-side restriction can distinguish them even if a volume-based calculation gives equal dimensional weights. Read the conditions of the eligible route and keep the three individual measurements in your notes rather than recording only the multiplication result.

sections.heading: Select units carefully on a mobile calculator
paragraphs: LoloBuy’s estimator labels the weight input in grams. If a warehouse record says 1.25 kg, enter 1,250 g. If your measuring tool is marked in millimetres, divide by ten to obtain centimetres. For example, 650 mm equals 65 cm. A value of 650 entered into a centimetre field describes a 6.5 m object and can hide eligible routes or produce misleading results.

For fractional measurements, note the figure you actually observed and follow the route or interface instructions on rounding. Do not round a side downward to sneak under a limit. A parcel very close to a stated maximum merits clarification from the warehouse or carrier before you commit to a plan. If a large end cap or irregular protrusion makes the true maximum unclear, measure the maximum outside span and ask what measurement the carrier will use.

Enter the final goods categories as accurately as the measurements. A box of artwork and a box with dense electronic accessories can have the same dimensions and gross weight but different eligible routes. LoloBuy’s form makes category a separate input for that reason. When the parcel contains the art book as well, check how the form expects the contents to be selected and whether all components are acceptable for the route you prefer.

sections.heading: Compare the cost of protection with the cost of damage
paragraphs: A rigid tube or reinforced carton may increase weight and dimensions. That does not automatically make it a poor choice. If the poster is difficult to replace or you need the gift to arrive undamaged for a particular date, a modestly larger parcel may be preferable. Describe the physical outcome you need, such as keeping the poster rolled and preventing the book corners from pressing against it. The warehouse can then tell you which packing arrangements are feasible.

If two packing proposals are available, compare them on the same basis. Note outer measurements, gross weight, packaging cost, contents and actual route. Plan A might give the lower freight result but require a separate paid packing service. Plan B might use an existing retail tube and a slightly larger ordinary carton. Count everything you would genuinely choose. Do not count a hypothetical discount unless the actual parcel qualifies for it.

If the combined package still exceeds your budget, consider whether the book can travel in a later parcel that is already planned. Calculate the extra cost that the book would add to that later parcel as well as the poster’s standalone cost. Putting the book “in the next shipment” does not make it free. It changes which parcel pays for the weight and space. If there is no actual future shipment, price a separate parcel rather than assuming one will appear.

sections.heading: Compare the final invoice with your trial
paragraphs: Once the warehouse supplies packed measurements, rerun the calculator and keep a screenshot of the inputs with the result. If the final amount differs, compare the exact dimensions, gross grams, route, destination and any optional charges. A higher cost can be entirely consistent with a different carton after reinforcement. If every visible input matches, ask which tariff condition or fee accounts for the difference.

Save the final real-world measurements privately for a future poster purchase. They can provide a better starting range than item-only dimensions, especially when the same seller uses a stable retail tube. Recheck every new parcel anyway. A thicker art book, another protective cap or a different destination can change the calculation while the poster itself stays the same.

If the seller can provide a photograph of its packed retail tube beside a ruler before purchase, use that to refine the starting estimate and label it as seller packaging. The international outer carton may still differ. Keeping the two measurements distinct makes a later difference understandable without assuming that either the seller or the warehouse measured incorrectly.

articles.title: A different variant reached LoloBuy: documenting a seller return before parcel submission
articles.description: Build a short evidence record that connects the seller’s option, the paid order and the warehouse item.

sections.heading: Establish what you ordered
paragraphs: A listing thumbnail shows a navy-and-white backpack. The selected variant is the navy body with a white front pocket. At the warehouse, the picture appears to show an all-navy backpack. Start with the variant confirmation on the paid order, not the thumbnail alone. A seller may use the same photo across several options, and translated names may differ from the labels used by the warehouse.

Save the original source option, the paid order and the current warehouse image. Note the relevant item number and date. If the colour difference could simply be lighting, look for a variant code, distinctive panel or other feature that distinguishes the two. If an entire panel is hidden in the image, request the missing angle before concluding the seller shipped the wrong variant.

sections.heading: Preserve the condition while checking eligibility
paragraphs: Read the current return action and any deadline for this item as soon as you discover the discrepancy. LoloBuy has a dedicated return procedure, while special manual orders can have seller-dependent restrictions. Promptly ask about available steps if the platform status and seller terms leave you uncertain. Do not assume free storage extends the time for a return.

Keep tags, packaging and included accessories intact. Postpone changes such as removing original packaging, combining the item into an international parcel or asking for alterations while a return remains under consideration. A service intended to reduce shipping size can compromise a seller return if you later establish a mismatch.

sections.heading: Request a specific outcome
paragraphs: A focused request might say “The paid option shows navy with a white front pocket. The warehouse front photo shows a navy pocket and the warehouse label reads [code]. Could you check whether the seller can exchange it for [correct code], and confirm any freight or service charge before proceeding?” Attach the two clearest images. Avoid burying the key detail in a long gallery.

If the seller offers an exchange, ask whether the replacement will be checked again and whether another deadline applies. If a return is accepted, follow the account record through dispatch back to the seller and any eventual credit. Acceptance of a request, physical return and a posted refund are different events. Save the reference for each.

sections.heading: Decide what the evidence shows before choosing a remedy
paragraphs: There are several plausible situations in the backpack example. The seller may have dispatched the wrong variant. The warehouse may have photographed the correct one under lighting that obscures the contrast. Or your paid order may show the all-navy variant despite the catalogue picture that led you to the listing. Each calls for a different next question. Start with the structured paid option and seller wording, then compare the evidence for the actual item. This avoids asking for an exchange that simply repeats the selection you already made.

If the order is wrong because the selection on the shopping page reset to a default, explain that accurately when asking whether a change is possible. If the seller supplied a clearly different model code, point to that mismatch. You need not decide who is at fault before asking staff to clarify the order. Describe what was requested, what arrived, and what evidence still needs confirmation. That precision often reduces the number of messages required to identify the problem.

Distinguish a wrong variant from a disagreement about a product description. If the paid order says “navy with white pocket” and the pocket is plainly navy, the variant check is straightforward. If the order says only “navy” while the listing photograph shows a light-coloured insert, the question is what was included in that seller option. Save the relevant source text and ask for clarification instead of treating a photo of optional styling as an unconditional promise.

sections.heading: Compare exchange, return and keeping the item
paragraphs: An exchange is useful only if the correct variant still exists, the replacement can arrive in time, and any additional domestic freight or service charge is acceptable. Ask whether a replacement would keep the same order reference or be processed as a new transaction. Track the replacement through warehouse receipt and check its variant again before assuming the first issue is resolved. A seller’s promise to send the correct model is a step forward, not evidence of what has arrived.

A return may make more sense when the desired version is unavailable or the timing no longer works. Ask which amount is eligible for refund, who pays any return freight and what condition the seller requires. The advertised item price and the total initially paid can differ because domestic freight or services were included. Do not assume every original payment component will be refunded. Use the current order terms and the platform’s confirmed response for the case.

Keeping the item can also be reasonable if the difference is minor and you still value the product. If the seller offers a partial adjustment, verify the exact amount, currency and where it would be credited. Consider whether accepting it would settle the issue and whether you are comfortable shipping the received variant internationally. Take the decision with the actual discrepancy in view, not under pressure from a presumed parcel deadline that the account has not confirmed.

sections.heading: Keep a sequence of events for the return
paragraphs: Record when the item was stored, when you first reported the mismatch, what the seller or platform requested and which action you took. If the procedure sets a deadline, use its stated starting event and time zone if shown. An international buyer can easily confuse the local time of a support message with the date the warehouse uses. Where a boundary is close, contact support promptly and ask for the deadline for that specific item rather than relying on an unofficial generalisation.

If a return is approved, retain the approval and any China-side return tracking. A seller may need to receive and inspect the returned goods before a credit is posted. Follow the actual record instead of assuming approval, completed shipment and final refund happen at once. If the credit arrives, compare its amount with the agreed remedy and keep track of whether it is account balance or an external payment movement.

If several similar backpacks were purchased, use the same item reference throughout. It is possible to compare the right evidence yet apply the return action to the wrong warehouse unit. Before confirming any action, read the source ID, colour option, size and warehouse record one more time. Mark the disputed unit as unavailable for international consolidation in your own plan until the case reaches a clear decision.

sections.heading: Receive the replacement as a new inspection decision
paragraphs: When a replacement reaches the warehouse, use the saved original specification and the seller’s correction confirmation. A second photo of a navy backpack taken from behind cannot settle whether the front pocket is white. Ask for the angle that distinguishes the two models. If the replacement now matches and its visible condition is acceptable, update the warehouse row and parcel plan with its new reference if one exists.

When reviewing your final costs, keep the original purchase, any return freight, refund or partial credit, and any replacement charge as separate entries. This produces an accurate record of what the resolution cost you and lets you explain it if a later transaction appears under a different reference. It also prevents a correct refund from being accidentally subtracted twice from the delivered price.
Keep that cost record with the final item reference if you later combine the replacement with goods from another seller.

articles.title: Combining LoloBuy warehouse items when one item can crush another
articles.description: Compare a combined parcel with separate shipments using a realistic packing arrangement and the value of each item’s protection.

sections.heading: Start with a compatibility check
paragraphs: Imagine a ceramic cup, a thick book and a folded tea towel from three sellers. LoloBuy allows selected stored goods to travel together. Choosing all three at once can reduce repeated packaging, but it also puts a hard moving object beside a breakable one. Before comparing prices, establish which arrangements can protect the cup and preserve the book’s corners.

A tea towel may soften contact but is not a substitute for reliable immobilisation or a suitable inner pack. Ask what protection the warehouse can offer, how it would separate the goods, and what that adds to weight and dimensions. If an item arrived with protective moulding, do not request its removal until you understand what would replace it.

sections.heading: Compare three complete parcel plans
paragraphs: Plan one sends everything in a single protected box. Plan two sends the cup separately and packs the book with the towel. Plan three, if appropriate, holds the towel for another order and sends the cup and book separately. For each plan, note every parcel, its realistic packed measurements, destination, eligible routes and optional service charges. Add the cost of all parcels you still intend to send.

If the combined estimate is lower by a small amount, ask what you give up to achieve it. It may depend on removing the inner carton that you want retained or using a route that cannot accept the contents. If the split estimate is higher, check whether better protection, different tracking or different timing is worth that amount to you.

sections.heading: Confirm the selected warehouse references
paragraphs: Before submission, cross-check the selected item numbers and the packing request. “Keep the moulded inner packaging on cup [reference]; please keep it separate from book [reference]” is more useful than “pack carefully.” Ask for confirmation if your decision depends on a particular service. Only the warehouse can confirm what it can provide for the actual items.

When the final parcel details become available, compare them with the plan you approved. A new carton can change the route choices. Keep pre-shipment pictures of the goods and their visible condition. If an item arrives damaged, photograph the outside, inner protection and affected item before discarding the packaging and consult the current reporting procedure.

sections.heading: Ask what the warehouse can physically achieve
paragraphs: The seller’s packaging and the warehouse’s outer packing do different jobs. A fitted insert may protect the cup inside its retail box, while an international carton must also stop that box from moving or being crushed by a heavy book. Before authorising removal of any packaging, identify which piece of protection is being discussed. A suggestion to discard a thin decorative sleeve differs from removing the only fitted insert around the handle.

Describe the failure you want to prevent. A heavy book sliding against a handle, for example, concentrates force on a vulnerable feature. A rigid divider or separate protected package might address it if the warehouse offers a suitable service. Simply surrounding both loose items with soft materials may leave room for movement. Ask for the warehouse’s actual proposal and any added cost rather than prescribing an unverified packing arrangement that may not be available.

A useful question is “Can the cup remain in its fitted inner box, with a barrier keeping the book off the box, and what would the outside dimensions and gross weight be?” If the answer is that a larger carton is needed, enter that carton into your comparison. If staff cannot confirm sufficient separation and the cup has real value to you, sending it independently is a concrete alternative to compare.

sections.heading: Put both the separate and combined prices on one page
paragraphs: Suppose a combined package would cost 36 hypothetical units in freight plus 4 for added protection. Two separate packages might cost 20 and 17 units, plus 3 for the cup’s protection. Both alternatives total 40. In that case the headline freight figure makes the combined parcel look cheaper even though the complete cost is equal. The sensible decision depends on protection, timing and route conditions. These amounts are examples chosen to illustrate comparison, not LoloBuy quotes.

If the parcel containing the book can travel on a cheaper route than the fragile parcel, verify that each quoted route accepts its actual contents. A single combined parcel may lose the cheaper route if the fragile item changes eligibility. Conversely, paying two route minimums can make separation costly. Which effect dominates depends on the actual measurements and returned routes. There is no reliable answer based solely on the fact that the items were bought from different sellers.

Check how you divided the packaging cost. If the book already has appropriate protection and that service is included in the 17-unit price, do not add it again. If a quote for the cup assumes its original box has been removed, it is not comparable with a combined quote that keeps the box. Write down what remains around each item in each scenario so the prices reflect equivalent or consciously different protection.

sections.heading: Compare deadlines and delivery evidence
paragraphs: The book and cup may be intended for different dates. Combining them makes the slower or unresolved item a dependency for both. If the cup is still waiting for a replacement due to a seller defect, consider shipping the ready book and towel while that issue is settled. If they are a single gift and you need them together, combining or deliberately coordinating two parcels may be worth more effort.

Delivery evidence can also differ. One parcel means one set of carrier events for several warehouse orders. Two parcels mean two separate journeys. Make a simple contents list for each, including the warehouse references and visible condition before packing. A delivery scan for the book does not prove the cup arrived if they were sent separately. If combined, a delivery scan confirms receipt of a parcel rather than the condition of each item inside.

If you choose an optional parcel service or protection offer, read the current terms for the exact package and goods. Do not assume a general service covers fragile contents or that a package described as reinforced has insurance. Ask specifically about the cup and the type of damage you are concerned about. Keep the protection terms and physical packing instructions distinct; they address different parts of the decision.

sections.heading: Review the first photos at delivery
paragraphs: Where the outer box is visibly crushed or punctured, document the outside before removing the inner packaging. When opening it, record the arrangement of the book, towel, fitted cup box and any divider. This makes it possible to describe which layer was damaged and whether the goods were still secured. Keep all relevant material while you check the current after-sales procedure.

If the cup is intact but its retail box is dented, the significance depends on what you purchased and told the warehouse to preserve. If the cup is cracked despite an undamaged outer box, the pre-shipment condition and internal protection become especially useful evidence. Report observations in their sequence rather than assigning a cause you did not witness. A careful before-and-after record is more persuasive and more accurate than a general statement that the whole parcel was damaged.

After a successful delivery, note which packing arrangement was actually used and whether it met your priorities. That experience can inform another ceramic order, but a different cup shape, thinner handle, heavier companion item or changed route can make a previous packing decision inappropriate. Revisit the physical compatibility each time you build a new parcel.

sources.title: Independent guide to LoloBuy packaging and routes

faq.q: What number should I save from a Weidian find?
faq.a: Keep the original Weidian itemID and seller URL beside the selected option. Save the later LoloBuy order and warehouse references separately.

faq.q: Can identical photos identify one seller listing?
faq.a: No. Compare the marketplace ID, seller, selected option and quantity on the current product page before treating two finds as equivalent.

faq.q: What does LoloBuy’s manual purchase form ask for?
faq.a: It lists the product link, name, specifications, notes, product pictures, CNY item price, freight to the warehouse and quantity.

faq.q: Does the manual purchase total include overseas freight?
faq.a: The form labels the amount as excluding international shipping. It has a separate field for delivery to the warehouse.

faq.q: How should I enter a seller’s bundle price?
faq.a: Confirm whether the quoted amount is per piece or per bundle, and check the quantity and displayed subtotal together before submitting.

faq.q: Can special third-party purchases have different return conditions?
faq.a: Yes. LoloBuy’s manual-order notice flags seller-dependent return or exchange limits, possible extra charges and the possibility that staff cannot place the order.

faq.q: Which units does LoloBuy’s shipping estimator use?
faq.a: Enter weight in grams and length, width and height in centimetres. Use the packed outside dimensions when you have them.

faq.q: How many end categories can I select in the estimator?
faq.a: The official estimator says up to three. Ask support how to quote a parcel with more relevant categories instead of omitting part of its contents.

faq.q: Why did a route disappear when I changed the contents?
faq.a: The available routes depend on the inputs. Read the returned route conditions and ask LoloBuy about your exact items if the reason is unclear.

faq.q: Do I enter the item's dimensions or the outer parcel’s dimensions?
faq.a: For a parcel estimate, use the external packed measurements. If only product measurements exist, mark the early result provisional.

faq.q: Can LoloBuy consolidate goods bought from different sellers?
faq.a: Yes. Its homepage describes consolidating purchases at its China warehouse and selecting stored products for one parcel.

faq.q: How long is LoloBuy’s advertised free warehouse storage?
faq.a: The official homepage advertises 180 days. Verify the applicable dates on your specific warehouse record.

faq.q: Does free storage extend a seller return deadline?
faq.a: Do not infer that from the storage period. Consult the current return procedure and the action available on your particular order.

faq.q: Are LoloBuy QC photos included?
faq.a: LoloBuy’s homepage advertises free inspection pictures. Check which views are included for the product and any charges for additional requests.

faq.q: Can LoloBuy verify the inside of a sealed collectible from its outer carton?
faq.a: An exterior photo supports checks of the visible label, seal and carton condition. It cannot establish all contents or functions inside the package.

faq.q: Does one photo mean every unit in a 1688 order was inspected?
faq.a: No. Check the stock-in method, sampling arrangements and actual number of units examined. Ask about quantity or individual checks when needed.

faq.q: What should I review before requesting shoe-box removal?
faq.a: Review the pair, labels, visible condition, seller return eligibility and the value of retaining the box. Read the current removal notice before authorising the service.

faq.q: How can I keep the box for just one pair in a group?
faq.a: Identify the pair by its warehouse item reference and explicitly ask to retain its original box. Confirm the instruction before packing.

faq.q: Can reducing parcel volume leave the freight price unchanged?
faq.a: Yes, depending on the selected route's billing method, gross weight and charge increments. Compare actual estimates using the two feasible packing plans.

faq.q: What evidence helps with a wrong variant at the warehouse?
faq.a: Save the selected seller option, paid order, warehouse reference and a clear warehouse photo showing the mismatch. Check eligibility before requesting a return or exchange.

faq.q: What should I keep if an item arrives damaged?
faq.a: Preserve outer and inner packaging, the item, its warehouse pictures and delivery record. Photograph the damage and follow the platform’s current after-sales instructions promptly.
